hints.title: Choice Limitation and Bit Encoding
hints.text: The pool contains at most twenty integers. Since integers cannot be chosen more than once, how can representing selected numbers as a compact bit sequence capture all game scenarios?

hints.title: Adversarial Winning Condition Invariant
hints.text: A player wins from state mask if any valid integer selection either immediately equals or exceeds desiredTotal, or leaves the opponent in an inescapable losing state.

hints.title: Bitmask Recursive Search Procedure
hints.text: Confirm total pool sum reaches desiredTotal. Traverse available numbers not marked in the bitmask. If picking number i wins directly or makes recursive call with updated mask return false, record state as true in memoization table. Otherwise return false.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input size or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N * 2^N) time and O(2^N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Exhaustive game-tree exploration explores 20! permutations, easily exceeding time limits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Memoizing over 2^n bitmask states reduces runtime to O(n * 2^n) time using O(2^n) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle early base cases (e.g. total sum check) and formulate bitmask memoization for game states.
